record.original_question: Let n ≥ 6 and 1 ≤ q ≤ floor(n/2)/2. If Ω ⊂ R^n is a connected open set and f ∈ W^{2,q}(Ω, R^n) is a homeomorphism, is it possible that the sets {Jf > 0} and {Jf < 0} both have positive measure?

evidence.quote: Open problem 12. Sign of the Jacobian for W2,p mappings: Let n ≥ 6 and 1 ≤ q ≤ [n/2]/2. Let Ω ⊂ R^n be connected open set and let f ∈ W2,q(Ω, R^n) be a homeomorphism. Is it possible that both sets {Jf > 0} and {Jf < 0} have positive measure?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $n \geq 6$ be an integer and let $q$ be a real number with $1 \leq q \leq \lfloor n/2 \rfloor / 2$. Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ be a connected open set and let $f \in W^{2,q}(\Omega, \mathbb{R}^n)$ be a homeomorphism onto its image. Denote by $J_f(x) = \det Df(x)$ the Jacobian determinant of $f$ (defined almost everywhere via the weak first derivatives). Determine whether it is possible that both of the sets
$$\{x \in \Omega : J_f(x) > 0\} \quad \text{and} \quad \{x \in \Omega : J_f(x) < 0\}$$
have positive Lebesgue measure. Equivalently, must the Jacobian of every such second-order Sobolev homeomorphism have a constant sign almost everywhere on $\Omega$?
artifact.status_search_result: The question is listed as an explicit open problem in a 2025 survey on the Ball–Evans approximation problem. While the analogous W^{1,p} sign-of-Jacobian problem has seen recent progress (e.g., Hencl–Vejnar's construction for p=1, n≥4, and positivity results for p>⌊n/2⌋), no resolution of the W^{2,q} version for n≥6 and 1≤q≤⌊n/2⌋/2 was found in the search.
